questions.stem: Bromine is an element in Group 7 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which of these is the formula for a molecule of bromine? A 2Br B $ \mathrm{B r^{2}} $ Br2 C D $ \mathrm{B r}_{2} $

parts.label: b
parts.text: A small amount of liquid bromine is placed in a gas jar containing air. The jar is then sealed. After two minutes, a brown gas is seen just above the surface of the liquid. After two hours, the whole gas jar is full of the brown gas. after two minutes after two hours

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Which of these is the process that causes the brown gas to fill the gas jar? A condensation B diffusion evaporation sublimation

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Explain, using the particle theory, the observations seen in the gas jar.

parts.label: c
parts.text: This apparatus is used to demonstrate the movement of ammonia gas and hydrogen chloride gas. The gases are given off by the solutions at each end of the tube. When the gases meet, they form a white solid. Which letter shows the position where the white solid forms? A B C D

questions.stem: Iron is a metal that has many uses. One problem with iron is that it can rust when exposed to air.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the two substances that must be present in air for iron to rust.

parts.label: b
parts.text: These are four methods of preventing iron from rusting painting oiling coating in plastic galvanising The table lists three items made from iron. Complete the table by giving the best method of preventing each item from rusting. You may use each method once, more than once or not at all.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which of these metals is used to galvanise iron? A aluminium B lead C tin D zinc

questions.stem: (a) The box shows some methods that can be used to separate mixtures. The table lists some separations. Complete the table by giving the best method for each separation. You may use each method once, more than once or not at all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When a mixture of ethanol and water is separated, two colourless liquids, A and B, are obtained. Liquid A is ethanol containing a small amount of water. Liquid B is pure water.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Describe a chemical test to show that liquid A contains water.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Describe a physical test to show that liquid B is pure water.

questions.stem: The Periodic Table consists of elements arranged in order of increasing atomic number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: What is meant by the term atomic number? A the number of neutrons in an atom B the number of protons in an atom C the number of protons plus the number of electrons in an atom D the number of protons plus the number of neutrons in an atom

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties. This is because their atoms contain the same number of A protons B neutrons C electrons in the outer shell D protons and neutrons

parts.label: b
parts.text: The elements in the periods of the Periodic Table show a change in properties across the period from left to right. The table gives information about some elements in Period 2. giant or molecular for structure high or low for melting point Complete the table by writing one of these words in each blank space. acidic or basic for acid-base character of the oxide

questions.stem: A student uses this apparatus to investigate the rate of reaction between an excess of magnesium and two different dilute acids, X and Y. This is the method given to the student. place 0.5g of magnesium ribbon into the conical flask use a measuring cylinder to add $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of dilute acid X and then replace the bung record the total volume of gas collected every 20 seconds for two minutes repeat the method using $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of dilute acid Y instead of dilute acid X in each experiment, keep the temperature the same and the magnesium in excess

parts.label: a
parts.text: The student decides to use a burette, rather than a measuring cylinder, to add the acid to the conical flask.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Using a burette would be an improvement only if another change is made to the method. State the other change needed to the method.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State the advantage of using a burette.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The table shows the student's results. Draw a curve of best fit for each set of points. Plot the results for each acid on the grid. Label each curve as acid X or acid Y.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how the curves show which acid has the greater concentration.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Use the graph to find the total volume of gas collected at 70s for acid X. Show on the graph how you obtained your answer.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The average (mean) rate of the reaction for acid Y can be calculated using the expression $\mathrm {a v e r a g e r a t e} = \frac {\mathrm {t o t a l v o l u m e o f g a s c o l l e c t e d}}{\mathrm {t i m e t o c o l l e c t t h e g a s}}$ Calculate the average rate, in $ cm^{3}/s $ , for the first 30s for acid Y.

questions.stem: Copper and iron are metals. They have the typical properties of metals, including a high melting point and good electrical conductivity.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Draw a labelled diagram to show the arrangement of the particles involved in the bonding within a metal.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Explain why metals have good electrical conductivity.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Suggest why some metals have high melting points.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Copper and iron both form compounds containing ions with a 2+ charge. Sodium hydroxide is used to distinguish between solutions containing $ \mathrm{C u}^{2+} $ and $ \mathrm{F e}^{2+} $ ions. What would be observed when aqueous sodium hydroxide is added separately to each solution?

parts.label: c
parts.text: Copper can be found naturally as a pure metal. Iron is found only in compounds and has to be extracted by chemical reactions.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Suggest why copper can be found as a pure metal.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: The most common method of extracting iron is by the reduction of iron(III) oxide in a blast furnace. The diagram shows a blast furnace. Write a chemical equation to show how carbon monoxide forms in the blast furnace. (1)

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: The equation for the reaction between iron(III) oxide and carbon monoxide is $\mathrm {F e} _ {2} \mathrm {O} _ {3} + 3 \mathrm {C O} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {F e} + 3 \mathrm {C O} _ {2}$ Explain which element is reduced in this reaction.

parts.label: c-iv
parts.text: Describe how molten slag forms in the blast furnace.

questions.stem: The diagram shows how a student attempts to prepare some hydrogen gas.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State why no hydrogen is produced.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Which of these pairs of chemicals could be used to safely prepare hydrogen? A copper and dilute sulfuric acid B gold and dilute hydrochloric acid C potassium and dilute hydrochloric acid D zinc and dilute sulfuric acid

parts.label: b
parts.text: In an experiment, the student then successfully prepares some hydrogen and measures the volume of hydrogen collected. She does the same experiment four times. The table shows her results.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Explain which experiment produces an anomalous result.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Calculate the average (mean) volume of hydrogen collected.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Give a reason why it is important for the student to repeat the experiment.

questions.stem: When iodine reacts with an excess of chlorine at $ - 8 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ , a compound forms. The percentage composition by mass of this compound is $\mathrm {I} = 5 4. 4 \% \quad \mathrm {C I} = 4 5. 6 \%$

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show, by calculation, that the empirical formula of this compound is $ \mathrm{I C I}_{3} $

parts.label: b
parts.text: The molecular formula of this compound is $ \mathrm{I}_{2} \mathrm{C l}_{6} $ $ \mathrm{I}_{2} \mathrm{C l}_{6} $ is a yellow solid at room temperature and forms a liquid when heated. A dynamic equilibrium exists in this liquid, represented by this equation. $\mathrm {I} _ {2} \mathrm {C l} _ {6} (\mathrm {I}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {I C l} _ {2} ^ {+} (\mathrm {I}) + \mathrm {I C l} _ {4} ^ {-} (\mathrm {I})$

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: When a reaction is in dynamic equilibrium, the forward and backward reactions occur at the same time. State two other features of a reaction that is in dynamic equilibrium.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Suggest why liquid $ \mathrm{I}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{6} $ conducts electricity, but solid $ \mathrm{I}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{6} $ does not.

questions.stem: Bromine, chlorine and iodine are halogens in Group 7 of the Periodic Table. The three halogens have similar chemical properties but different reactivities.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A teacher uses this apparatus to demonstrate the difference in reactivity between these halogens. The teacher does each experiment in a fume cupboard. The table shows the observation for each halogen.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Suggest why the teacher uses a fume cupboard.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Use the information in the table to explain the order of reactivity of the three halogens.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: A student states that the order of reactivity cannot be found from this experiment because bromine is a liquid, chlorine is a gas and iodine is a solid at room temperature. Evaluate the student's statement.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Bromine, chlorine and iodine all react with hydrogen. In each reaction, a hydrogen halide (HX) is formed, where X represents the halogen.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for the reaction between hydrogen and bromine.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Draw a dot and cross diagram to represent a molecule of hydrogen chloride, HCl. Show only the outer shell electrons.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Name the solution formed when hydrogen chloride dissolves in water.

questions.stem: A student uses this apparatus to find the mass of magnesium oxide that forms when a strip of magnesium ribbon is burned in air. This is the student's method. weigh an empty crucible and lid place a coiled strip of freshly cleaned magnesium ribbon in the crucible weigh the crucible, lid and ribbon heat the crucible strongly for several minutes, lifting the lid and quickly replacing it several times leave the crucible, lid and contents to cool and then reweigh

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the appearance of the freshly cleaned magnesium ribbon and the appearance of the magnesium oxide that forms. magnesium ribbon magnesium oxide

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Explain why the student lifts the lid and quickly replaces it several times during the experiment. lifts lid replaces lid

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the mass of oxygen required to completely react with 0.6 g of magnesium to form magnesium oxide. The equation for the reaction is $2 \mathrm {M g} + \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {M g O}$

parts.label: c
parts.text: The mass of magnesium oxide that forms is less than expected. This could be because some of the magnesium reacts with nitrogen to form magnesium nitride, $ \mathrm{M g_{3} N_{2}} $ Write a chemical equation for the reaction between magnesium and nitrogen to form magnesium nitride.

questions.stem: The alkanes are a homologous series of hydrocarbons. The cycloalkanes are another homologous series of hydrocarbons, where the carbon atoms are arranged in a ring structure. Cyclopropane is the simplest cycloalkane. It can be represented as The tables give the names and molecular formulae of the first three members of each series.

parts.label: a
parts.text: One feature of a homologous series is that each member has the same general formula.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: What is the general formula for the homologous series of alkanes? A $ C_{n} H_{n} $ B $ C_{n} H_{2 n-2} $ C $ C_{n} H_{2 n} $ D $ C_{n} H_{2 n+2} $

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: What is the general formula for the homologous series of cycloalkanes? Use the information from the cycloalkane table to help you answer the question. A $ C_{n} H_{n} $ B $ C_{n} H_{2 n-2} $ C $ C_{n} H_{2 n} $ D $ C_{n} H_{2 n+2} $

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: State two other features of a homologous series of compounds.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Alkanes and cycloalkanes are saturated hydrocarbons.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State what is meant by the term saturated.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Draw the displayed formula for ethane, $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{6}} $

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: The displayed formula for cyclopropane is Draw a displayed formula for cyclobutane, $ \mathrm{C_{4} H_{8}} $

parts.label: c
parts.text: The reaction between cyclopropane and bromine is similar to the reaction between methane and bromine. One product of the reaction between cyclopropane and bromine is hydrogen bromide, HBr.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: State the condition required for this reaction to occur.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Complete the displayed formula for the other product of this reaction.

questions.stem: A student is given a mixture of two solid ionic compounds, A and B. Each solid contains one cation and one anion. Compound A is insoluble in water. Compound B is soluble in water.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how the student could separate the mixture to obtain solid A and a solution of B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The table shows the results of two tests the student does on a solution of B.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Use the information in the table to identify the cation and the anion present in compound B. cation anion

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Identify the gas given off in test 1.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student adds dilute hydrochloric acid to solid A. A gas that turns limewater milky is given off.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Explain which anion is present in solid A.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Give a test to show that solid A contains calcium ions.

questions.stem: This apparatus can be used to find the volume of dilute sulfuric acid needed to neutralise 25.0 $ cm^{3} $ of aqueous sodium hydroxide, NaOH.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how to use the apparatus to find the volume of dilute sulfuric acid needed to neutralise the sodium hydroxide. Assume that the apparatus is clean and does not need rinsing.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The volume of dilute sulfuric acid needed can also be found by measuring the highest temperature reached when the two solutions are mixed. In a series of experiments, different volumes of dilute sulfuric acid are added separately to $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ samples of aqueous sodium hydroxide. The graph shows the highest temperatures in each experiment. In each reaction, the starting temperatures of the two solutions are the same. $^{\circ} C$ Volume of acid added in $ \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ Use the graph to answer these questions.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State the starting temperature of each experiment. starting temperature = ... $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Find the volume of acid required to exactly neutralise the sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Find the two different volumes of acid that produce an increase in temperature of $ 1 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}. $

questions.stem: Lithium is an element in Group 1 of the Periodic Table. Lithium is stored in oil to prevent it from coming into contact with air and water.

parts.label: a
parts.text: When a piece of lithium is removed from the oil, dried and cut, the exposed surface A bubbles and fizzes B changes from shiny to dull C bursts into flame D does not change

parts.label: b
parts.text: When lithium is added to cold water in a beaker, hydrogen forms.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State the test for hydrogen.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: A few drops of phenolphthalein indicator are added to the solution in the beaker. Explain why the phenolphthalein turns pink.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The table shows some information about lithium oxide and lithium carbonate. Complete the table by giving the two missing formulae.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Caesium is another element in Group 1 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: The table below lists some statements about the reaction of caesium with cold water compared to the reaction of lithium with cold water. Place ticks ( $ \checkmark $ ) in the boxes to show the two correct statements.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for the reaction of caesium with water.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of HBr in $ 2 0. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the hydrobromic acid solution.

parts.label: b
